short: The 1868 decree abolishing the shogunate and returning government to the throne after 675 years.
full:
Shogun Tokugawa Yoshinobu had already offered to resign his authority in November 1867, expecting to keep the substance of power inside a council of lords. On 3 January 1868 forces from Satsuma and Chōshū seized the gates of the Kyoto palace and had the fifteen-year-old emperor issue the decree of ōsei fukko, the restoration of imperial rule, abolishing the shogunate and the regency and stripping Yoshinobu of his lands and offices.

The Tokugawa did not accept it quietly. The Boshin War ran from Toba-Fushimi later that month to the surrender of the last holdouts in Hokkaido in June 1869. Meanwhile the new government issued the Charter Oath in April 1868, moved the capital from Kyoto to Tokyo, and in 1871 abolished the domains outright, replacing 260 hereditary lords with prefectures under appointed governors. The samurai class was dismantled within a decade, its last armed protest crushed at Shiroyama in 1877. A restoration in name, it was the most thorough revolution in Japanese history.
